title: Fellow trombonists in Little Rock and finding his own style
summary: Happy Johnson and Will Parish are the only trombonists around; he practises day and night to avoid copying anyone, and the bandmaster raps him for adding notes.

people.name: Mr. Cook (Gibbs High School band master)

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: WAS ANYBODY ELSE IN HIGH SCHOOL WITH YOU. OR ANYBODY ELSE LIKE THAT IN HIGH SCHOOL WITH YOU?
No but I knew , he had played with

Yes, he's older than I am. But another guy, Happy Johnson, a trombone player. We both picked bones the same day. He only lived about two blocks from my house in Little Rock. He got to be a pretty good name.
HE DID PRETTY WELL OUT IN CALIFORNIA.

SO IN OTHER WORDS, WHEN YOU WERE IN HIGH SCHOOL NOW, YOU HAD TO DEVELOP YOUR OWN STYLE BECAUSE I DON'T THINK THERE WAS ANYBODY ELSE AROUND THEN--NO OUTSTANDING TROMBONE PLAYER IN LITTLE ROCK WAS THERE AT THAT TIME.
Well-, there was a guy with the Rose City Orchestra called Saxton. His real name was Will Parish.
HE CAME HERE TO PLAY WITH CHICK WEBBLATER?
Yeah, he did play with Chick awhile.
HE WAS INSIDE ROSE CITY ORCHESTRA?
Yeah-, right-, he had later became a Red Cap down here.

No, he died. He is about the only trombone player that I liked. Although I did not try to copy after him. In fact, I was determined, when I picked up the trombone, to do my own thing. I was determined not to play like anybody; so, I just practiced day and night. In fact, I practiced so much that they thought I was going to go nuts. So they took me off the instrument for a time.
WHAT OPPORTUNITIES DID YOU HAVE TO PLAY WHEN YOU WRE IN SCHOOL? DID YOU HAVE MUCH OPPORTUNITY TO PLAY OTHER THAN PRACTICE OR WERE YOU PLAYING TYPICAL SCHOOL...

Well, we were playing typical band music. I never forget a time that I put a couple of extra notes in this band music and Mr. Cook, the band master, hit me over my head with a baton. I shall never forget that. But, I always wanted to be what we call swing. I always wanted to do that.
